title: Immunoglobulin G (IgG)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: IgG is one of the main antibodies the immune system makes to fight germs. An immunoglobulins blood test measures the amount of IgG and other antibodies in the blood.
context: This test alone cannot diagnose a condition, so results outside the usual range often need more testing. Certain medicines can affect the result, and levels that are not normal do not always mean a condition that needs care.
aboveRange: Higher levels may be associated with an autoimmune condition
May be associated with a chronic infection
May be associated with some liver conditions, such as hepatitis or cirrhosis
May be associated with certain cancers of the blood, bone marrow, or immune system
belowRange: Lower levels may be associated with conditions that reduce protein in the body, such as some kidney conditions, serious burns, malabsorption, or malnutrition
May be associated with a condition affecting the ability to make immunoglobulins
May be associated with a genetic condition present from birth
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
